name: Assisted One-Arm Pull-Up
description: The assisted one-arm pull-up uses a band or the free hand lightly touching the working arm's wrist to reduce the load while training the full range of motion required for a strict one-arm pull-up. It develops the extreme lat, biceps, and forearm strength needed for one of the most demanding upper-body pulling movements in calisthenics.

execution.starting_position: Grip the bar with one hand in the center. The free hand can lightly grip the working wrist or a looped band is placed under the working knee/foot. Begin in a dead hang.
execution.setup_instructions: Method 1: Loop a thin band around the bar and place one foot in it — provides variable resistance assistance. Method 2: Lightly touch the working arm's wrist with the fingertips of the free hand. Use only minimal assistance.
steps: Step 1: Begin hanging from one arm, opposite hand providing minimal assistance.
Step 2: Depress and retract the working shoulder blade.
Step 3: Pull the chest toward the bar by driving the working elbow down.
Step 4: Continue until the chin clears the bar.
Step 5: Lower under control — the eccentric is as valuable as the concentric.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale aggressively on the pull. Inhale on the controlled descent.
common_mistakes: Applying too much assistance — use the minimum needed to complete clean reps
Skipping negatives — the eccentric is essential for strength development
safety_considerations: Prerequisites: 15+ unassisted pull-ups. Progress extremely slowly.
High risk of elbow tendinopathy if volume is excessive — limit to 3-5 reps per side per session
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full dead hang to chin above bar.
coaching_cues: Use only a fingertip's worth of assistance
Own every inch of the descent
Keep the free arm close — do not reach across the body
